source.title: Hydrogel Matrix to Support Stem Cell Survival After Brain Transplantation in Stroke

material: Hyaluronan–heparin–collagen hydrogel (HyStem-HP) with embryonic cortex-derived NPCs

formulation.evidence: 100 000 neuronal stem cells in 1 mL were mixed with 4 mL hyaluronan/heparin sulfate, 1 mL gelatin, and 1 mL cross-linker to form a stem-cell–hydrogel complex.

biology.cell_type: GFP mouse neural progenitor cells derived from E12.5 embryonic cortex

other_outcomes.evidence: 1.20 ± 0.15 mm without hydrogel vs 1.56 ± 0.35 mm with hydrogel; P = .22
other_outcomes.name: peri-infarct PECAM-positive vessel length

other_outcomes.evidence: ratio of optical density [OD] between peri-infarct and contralateral area was 5.63 ± 1.34 without hydrogel vs 5.82 ± 0.68 with hydrogel; P = .92
other_outcomes.name: GFAP OD ratio peri-infarct/contralateral

other_outcomes.evidence: 1.25 ± 0.18 mm³ without hydrogel vs 1.18 ± 0.35 mm³ with hydrogel; P = .77
other_outcomes.name: infarct size with hydrogel

survival.evidence: Cells transplanted with hydrogel had an average of 8000 cells—a statistically significant 2-fold expansion in cell survival (P = .035).

notes: Commercial HyStem-HP: thiol-modified sodium hyaluronate, heparin sulfate, gelatin, cross-linked with PEG diacrylate. Injected into photothrombotic stroke cavity 7 days post-stroke in C57BL/6 mice; cells-only control had 4000 surviving cells. In vitro, hydrogel increased survival (LDH, CCK-8) under B27/bFGF deprivation at 24 h; values only in figures. Iba1+ microglia infiltration significantly decreased (P = .004).
